Cards and contactless are widely accepted in cities. Keep small local notes for markets, tips and rural transport.

faq.q: How much cash should I carry?
faq.a: Enough for one or two days, not more. Use bank ATMs inside branches, decline the machine's own currency conversion, and split cash across two places.

faq.q: Is a travel eSIM or a local SIM better?
faq.a: An eSIM works before you land and needs no shop visit. A local SIM is often cheaper per gigabyte. Compare both against your trip length and data needs.

faq.q: Do I need a local SIM to use my phone abroad?
faq.a: Only if your plan does not include roaming. Data roaming can cost many times more than a local or eSIM plan.

faq.q: How early should I book flights?
faq.a: Book 4 to 8 weeks ahead for most routes. Peak holidays and long-haul flights get expensive much earlier; check the local school holiday calendar first.

faq.q: What is the cheapest way to get from the airport?
faq.a: Usually the scheduled airport bus or the rail link. Compare the total door-to-door time, not just the ticket price, and check when the last service runs.
Yes. Cover medical treatment, trip cancellation and lost luggage, and check that your destination has adequate healthcare before you rely on it.

faq.q: How do I avoid jet lag?
faq.a: Shift your sleep by 1 to 2 hours per day before you fly, eat on the destination's schedule once you land, and get daylight early.

faq.q: What vaccinations or health checks do I need?
faq.a: Requirements change. Check your government's travel health site and a clinic 4 to 8 weeks before departure.
It depends on the country. Some places add a service charge; others round up or tip in cash. Check local norms and never tip if a menu says service is included.

faq.q: How do I get around at night when public transport has stopped?
faq.a: Plan a backup before you need one: an official taxi number, a ride-hail app that works there, or your hotel's shuttle. Agree the price before you set off.

faq.q: Should I book accommodation before I arrive?
faq.a: Yes for the first night, and for the whole trip in peak season or during events. Free cancellation is the safest option.

faq.q: How do I find free things to do?
faq.a: Look for free museum days, public parks, walking routes, viewpoints and community events. City tourism offices publish a free-events calendar.
Passport with 6+ months validity, visa or entry permit where required, insurance details, and offline copies of every booking. Keep a digital and a paper copy.
